trial.title: SAbR For Oligometastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma

endpoints.measure: Time to start of systemic therapy (TTST)
endpoints.description: To evaluate the delay in time to start of systemic therapy (TTST) as a surrogate of progression free survival (PFS), defined as the time from the first day of SAbR to start of systemic therapy.

endpoints.measure: Modified progression-free survival (mPFS) for patients who are treated with SAbR
endpoints.description: Modified progression-free survival (mPFS) for patients with oligometastatic renal cell carcinoma who are treated with SAbR. Modified progression-free survival (mPFS) is defined as the survival interval without development of \>3 sites of new metastasis, new sites of metastases that are not amenable to SAbR treatment, a total of \>6 sites of metastasis that required SAbR, local failure at SAbR-treated site, or development of brain metastasis, with the definition of new metastasis and local failure (progression) as defined by RECIST. "Metastasis" in this entire protocol refers to extra-cranial metastasis unless otherwise specified.

To evaluate progression on next line of systemic therapy as defined by RECIST 1.1 starting from mPFS (modified progression free survival). Response and progression will be evaluated in this study using the new international criteria proposed by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v 1.1) Committee \[Eur J Cancer. 2009;45(2):228-247\]. Changes in only the largest diameter (unidimensional measurement) of the tumor lesions are used in the RECIST v1.1 criteria.
Overall survival (OS), which is defined as the time between date of registration and the date of death due to any cause.
Cancer specific survival is defined as the time between date of registration and the date of death due to renal cell carcinoma.
Radiographic progression with \>30% increase in the longest diameter of the treated lesions.

Median response duration is defined as the time between the date a response (CR or PR) was first seen until date of progression. Response and progression will be evaluated in this study using the new international criteria proposed by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST v 1.1) Committee \[Eur J Cancer. 2009;45(2):228-247\]. Changes in only the largest diameter (unidimensional measurement) of the tumor lesions are used in the RECIST v1.1 criteria.

endpoints.measure: Time to development of new lesions
endpoints.description: Interval time to development of new lesions that can be treated with additional local therapy- title would be this or a shortened version of it. Time to event will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier approach along with the 95% confidence interval.

endpoints.measure: Time to disease progression that cannot be treated
endpoints.description: To measure the time interval from registration to time to disease progression that cannot be treated with further local therapy and need to initiate or switch systemic therapy. Time to event will be estimated using the Kaplan-Meier approach along with the 95% confidence interval.

Severity or Toxicity will be assessed according to the National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Toxicity Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), version 5.0. Dose adjustments should be made according to the system showing the greatest degree of toxicity. The consequences of toxicity should all be graded 1-5 according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), version 5.0 occurring prior to 270 days from the start of protocol treatment. Other treatment related toxicity attributed to the therapy will be captured, recorded and the consequences of should all be graded 1-5 according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE). CTCAE V5.0 along with grades 1-5.

HRQOL will be measured using FACT-G questionnaire at baseline and at first follow up 8-12 weeks (+/- 4 weeks) then 12 week (±4 week) intervals for 1 year, and every 26 weeks (±4 weeks) until the completion of follow ups. FACT-G is a measure that sums the functional well being (FWB), physical well being (PWB), the social/family well-being (S/FWB), and emotional well being (EMB).

HRQOL will be measured using EQ-5D (EuroQol- 5 Dimension) questionnaire at baseline and at first follow up 8-12 weeks (+/- 4 weeks) then 12 week (±4 week) intervals for 1 year, and every 26 weeks (±4 weeks) until the completion of follow ups. EQ-5D-5L is a self-assessed, health related, quality of life questionnaire. The scale measures quality of life on a 5-component scale including mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression.

HRQOL will be measured using FKSI questionnaire at baseline and at first follow up 8-12 weeks (+/- 4 weeks) then 12 week (±4 week) intervals for 1 year, and every 26 weeks (±4 weeks) until the completion of follow ups. FKSI adds to the FACT-G (27 items) by including 15 items specific to kidney cancer patients. In a HRQOL study focused on patient with mRCC, a symptoms subscale questionnaire was developed and will also be administered in this study.

Health care utilization data needed to assess costs will be obtained from the cost \& convenience questionnaire, which includes costs of hospitalization, treatment, ER visits, physician and clinic visits and medications. Markov modeling with probabilistic sensitivity analysis will be used to correlate quality-adjusted survival and cost. Cost-effective analysis (cost \& convenience questionnaire) will be given prior to treatment and at the time of progression.

outcome.rationale: Phase II single-arm SAbR trial expected to meet primary TTST endpoint and secondary local control endpoint based on established efficacy of SBRT in oligometastatic disease. Modified PFS and OS outcomes uncertain but likely favorable in selected population. Safety profile expected acceptable. HRQOL and cost-effectiveness exploratory.

value.estimand: Single-arm SAbR-treated patients; time from first SAbR to initiation of systemic therapy; measured at 1 year
value.uncertainty: No direct Phase II data for SAbR monotherapy in oligometastatic RCC; estimate based on oligometastatic SBRT literature and RCC retrospective series
value.rationale: SAbR delays systemic therapy in oligometastatic RCC. Meta-analyses of oligometastatic SBRT show median time to next therapy 6-12 months. Favorable-risk population (≤3 mets, ECOG ≤1) supports 9-12 month median TTST prediction.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: SAbR provides durable local control delaying need for systemic therapy in selected oligometastatic RCC patients.

value.estimand: Single-arm SAbR-treated patients; modified PFS (no >3 new mets, no unresectable new mets, no >6 total mets requiring SAbR, no local failure, no brain mets); measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Modified PFS definition unique to this trial; no direct comparable data; estimate extrapolated from oligometastatic SBRT PFS data
value.rationale: Modified PFS incorporates strict criteria for progression. SBRT for oligometastatic disease shows median PFS 6-12 months; favorable definition may extend this. Conservative estimate 10-14 months.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: Modified PFS captures disease control beyond conventional PFS; SAbR expected to delay progression events.

value.estimand: Patients starting next line of systemic therapy; PFS on systemic therapy per RECIST 1.1; measured from mPFS over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Highly variable based on when systemic therapy initiated and regimen used; no specific data for post-SAbR systemic therapy PFS in RCC
value.rationale: PFS on subsequent systemic therapy depends on timing of SAbR failure and choice of therapy. Contemporary RCC systemic therapies (TKI/IO) show 8-12 month median PFS; prior treatment may affect response.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: Post-SAbR systemic therapy PFS depends on disease biology and treatment selection; moderate expectation of benefit.

value.estimand: All registered patients; time from registration to death from any cause; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Oligometastatic RCC prognosis highly variable; favorable-risk patients may have extended survival; limited prospective SAbR-specific OS data
value.rationale: Oligometastatic RCC with ≤3 lesions and good performance status has favorable prognosis. Historical 2-year OS 60-80% in similar populations. SAbR may improve outcomes through durable local control.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: OS expected to be favorable in selected oligometastatic RCC patients treated with SAbR.

value.estimand: All registered patients; time from registration to death from RCC; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: CSS similar to OS in RCC as most deaths are disease-related; limited SAbR-specific prospective data
value.rationale: In metastatic RCC, most deaths are disease-related. CSS expected to be slightly higher than OS. Favorable-risk oligometastatic population supports 2-year CSS estimate of 75%.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: CSS expected to be favorable in oligometastatic RCC with SAbR providing effective local control.

value.estimand: SAbR-treated lesions; local control defined as absence of >30% increase in longest diameter; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: SAbR for RCC metastases shows high local control in retrospective series; dose fractionation varies; some heterogeneity by metastasis site
value.rationale: SBRT/SABR for RCC metastases consistently demonstrates high local control rates (80-95% at 1-2 years) across multiple retrospective series. Ablative doses used in this protocol (≥25Gy x1, ≥12Gy x3, ≥8Gy x5) should achieve similar results.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: SAbR provides excellent local control for RCC metastases with ablative dosing.

value.estimand: Responders (CR or PR per RECIST 1.1); time from first response to progression; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Response rate to SAbR in RCC oligometastases unknown; duration of response highly variable; limited prospective data
value.rationale: SAbR can induce CR/PR in treated lesions but response rate variable. Duration depends on development of new metastases vs local control. Estimate based on time to new lesions or progression in oligometastatic SBRT series.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: Response duration reflects durability of SAbR effect; expected to be moderate given risk of new metastases.

value.estimand: All patients; time to development of new lesions amenable to additional local therapy; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Time to new lesions depends on disease biology; oligometastatic state may represent transitional phenotype; limited RCC-specific data
value.rationale: In oligometastatic RCC, time to new lesion development varies widely. Some patients remain oligometastatic for years; others progress rapidly. Median estimate 6-12 months based on natural history and SBRT series.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: Time to new lesions reflects disease progression; SAbR may delay by controlling existing disease.

value.estimand: All patients; time to progression not amenable to further local therapy requiring systemic therapy switch; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: Definition overlaps with TTST and mPFS; estimate similar to TTST but may be longer if some new lesions can be treated with additional SAbR
value.rationale: This endpoint captures when disease becomes too extensive for local therapy alone. Expected to be similar to or slightly longer than TTST if repeat SAbR allowed for new lesions. Estimate 9-14 months.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: Time to polymetastatic progression reflects benefit of SAbR in delaying systemic therapy need.

value.estimand: All treated patients; Grade 3+ toxicity per CTCAE v5.0; acute (≤90 days) and delayed (>90 days) toxicity; measured over 6 years
value.uncertainty: SAbR generally well-tolerated; toxicity varies by site (bone, lung, liver, adrenal); RCC metastases often in challenging locations (adrenal, bone)
value.rationale: SBRT/SABR for oligometastatic disease shows Grade 3+ toxicity rates of 5-15% in most series. RCC metastases may involve adrenal glands and bone requiring careful dosing. Expected toxicity rate 5-15%.

endpoint_predictions.rationale: SAbR toxicity expected to be manageable with appropriate patient selection and dosing.

value.rationale: FACT-G scores may improve slightly with effective local control of metastases but decline with disease progression. Limited specific data for RCC SAbR. Conservative estimate of minimal change.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT02956798 is a Phase II single-arm study of SAbR for oligometastatic RCC (≤3 metastases). Primary endpoint: Time to start of systemic therapy (TTST) at 1 year. Secondary endpoints include modified PFS, OS, CSS, local control, response duration, time to new lesions, toxicity, and HRQOL measures.

Evidence base: Limited direct evidence for SAbR monotherapy in oligometastatic RCC. Meta-analyses of SBRT/SABR for oligometastatic disease across tumor types suggest local control rates of 70-90% and median PFS of 6-12 months. RCC-specific data from retrospective series and small prospective studies indicate SAbR can achieve durable local control in selected oligometastatic patients.

Population match: Oligometastatic RCC (≤3 lesions), extrapulmonary sites allowed, no brain mets, ECOG ≤1, prior systemic therapy allowed if >1 year ago. This represents favorable-risk oligometastatic population.

Key uncertainty: No direct Phase II data for SAbR monotherapy in this exact population; expected completion 2025-12-30 per protocol. Evidence relies on indirect data from mixed oligometastatic populations and RCC-specific retrospective series.

Primary endpoint (TTST): Expected to show delay in initiation of systemic therapy. Historical data suggests median time to systemic therapy of 6-12 months in similar populations. Predicted median TTST: 9-12 months.
mPFS endpoints: Modified PFS incorporating local failure and new lesion development. Expected median mPFS 10-14 months based on oligometastatic SBRT literature.
OS/CSS: Oligometastatic RCC has variable prognosis; 2-year OS estimated 60-75% in favorable-risk patients.
Local control: SAbR for RCC metastases typically achieves 80-90% local control at 1-2 years.
Toxicity: SAbR generally well-tolerated; Grade 3+ toxicity expected <15%.
HRQOL: Expected stable or improved scores post-SAbR in responders; limited specific data for RCC.
